title: Sr. Software Engineer, Cloud Platform
description: Who we are Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term. About the role: As a Senior Engineer in the Infrastructure org, you will help evolve the cloud foundations behind every Samsara product. Your goal will be to reduce systemic production risk and enable continued growth by making infrastructure safer to change, easier to operate, and more resilient and cost-efficient at scale. You will bring deep expertise in at least one infrastructure domain, such as compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud control planes, and apply it across our multi-account, multi-region AWS environment. You will lead work such as modernizing compute and stateful infrastructure, strengthening capacity and failure isolation, and building standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation. You will partner with product engineering teams to turn recurring risks and manual operations into durable platforms and paved paths. We do not expect you to be an expert in every infrastructure domain. We are looking for engineers who have built and operated critical systems at significant scale, understand how infrastructure fails, and can use that experience to improve both our platforms and our engineering practices. You should apply if: You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely. You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go. You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes. You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we're all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win together. In this role, you will:   Design, build, and operate reliable cloud platforms, bringing depth in one or more areas such as compute, networking, storage, stateful systems, or infrastructure control planes. Improve the scalability, capacity management, isolation, recovery, and cost efficiency of critical production infrastructure. Build standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation that support self-service provisioning, testing, progressive rollout, reconciliation, rollback, and drift prevention.  Identify shared failure modes and build safeguards that prevent localized failures from escalating into broad customer impact. Contribute to multi-account, multi-region, and isolated AWS architectures,

title: Senior Asset Pipeline Engineer, Sim-Ready Content
description: About Genesis AI Genesis AI builds the simulation platform powering the next generation of robotics and embodied AI. Our flagship product, Genesis World, is a unified multi-physics simulation engine paired with Nyx, our in-house GPU-accelerated, path-traced photorealistic renderer. Together they provide a platform for training robotics and embodied AI at scale; letting teams simulate complex physical worlds with high fidelity and speed, from a laptop to datacenter-grade GPUs, and close the gap between simulation and the real world. About the Role A simulator is only as useful as the content that runs inside it. Training embodied agents at scale means large volumes of assets that are simultaneously physically valid and visually convincing and that is a pipeline problem before it is an art problem. We're hiring a Senior Engineer to build the path from raw input to sim-ready asset: geometry from a range of sources going in; clean meshes, correct collision proxies, plausible physical properties, materials that hold up under a path tracer, and reliable metadata coming out. The bar is throughput and repeatability. An asset that needs a human pass to be usable doesn't scale, so the pipeline has to make good decisions on its own and flag the cases where it can't. Part of that autonomy comes from agents embedded in the graph itself. Nodes can call models to produce input content, drive generation, pick parameters, interpret a mesh before deciding how to treat it, or judge whether a result is acceptable. Making that reliable is its own engineering problem: agents are non-deterministic, they fail in ways a mesh operator doesn't, and they need guardrails, structured outputs, retries and verification around them. You'll be building that as a first-class part of the pipeline rather than bolting it on. You'll work closely with the stakeholders, who set direction and priorities. You own the technical design and the implementation and you're expected to bring enough pipeline experience to challenge the plan where it needs challenging. What You'll Do Build and maintain the end-to-end asset pipeline, from ingestion through to validated output Design agent-driven nodes that generate input content and make decisions inside the graph, with the structured outputs, guardrails and fallbacks that make them dependable in batch Develop automated processing stages: mesh repair, retopology, decimation and LODs, UV unwrapping and texel density normalization, collision proxy generation Derive physical properties so assets behave correctly in simulation: mass, inertia, contact parameters, articulation setup Handle appearance: material conversion to PBR, texture processing, baking, and color management so assets render correctly in Nyx Define and enforce asset standards (units, orientation, pivots, naming, provenance) and build the validators that reject noncompliant assets before they reach the library Scale the pipeline to large batch runs, with caching, versioning and selective reprocessing when a stage changes Build quality checks into the pipeline itself: physics stability harnesses, render smoke tests, automated evaluation of generated content, comparison on reprocessed assets Work with the rendering, physics and research teams on what sim-ready needs to mean for each downstream use What We're Looking For (ideally) 5+ years building content or asset pipelines in games, VFX, simulation, or 3D tooling, with ownership of a pipeline in production Deep knowledge of 3D asset formats and their quirks: USD, glTF, FBX, OBJ, plus physics description formats such as URDF or MJCF Strong Python and C++ where processing needs to be fast Hands-on mesh processing expertise: remeshing, decimation, UV generation, repair operations, convex decomposition, and a clear sense of how each one fails Solid command of PBR material authoring, texture baking and color spaces Experience driving DCC tools headlessly (Blender, Houdini, Maya) and building batch or distributed job system

title: Werkstudent Go-To-Market & Partner Management (m/w/d)
tags_raw: Operations; Internship; Deutsch; CRM; Hubspot; Process; SaaS; sales
description: Deine Mission Das Produkt steht. Jetzt entscheidet sich, wie wir darüber sprechen. Das ist kein Callcenter-Job. Keine Kaltakquise, keine gekaufte Liste, keine Quote pro Stunde. Du kontaktierst Betriebe, die uns bereits kennen. Installationspartner, mit denen wir seit Monaten oder Jahren arbeiten. Sie wissen, wer Bees & Bears ist — sie wissen nur noch nicht, was wir gerade Neues für sie gebaut haben. Warum es diese Stelle gibt: Wir bringen ein neues Produkt an den Start, das unseren Partnerbetrieben einen konkreten Engpass löst. Technisch ist es fertig. Was jetzt zählt, ist die Einführung — und die passiert nicht über eine Mail. Sie passiert in Gesprächen. Deine Aufgabe: Diese Gespräche führen. Du bekommst eine Einarbeitung und einen Gesprächsleitfaden. Nach acht Wochen sollte auch dieser Leitfaden noch besser sein, weil du hundert Gespräche geführt hast. Wer nur die Liste abarbeiten will, ist hier falsch. Wer wartet, bis jemand den nächsten Schritt vorgibt, auch. Wohin die Rolle wächst: Sie startet fokussiert: ein Produkt, ein definierter Partnerkreis, ein Gespräch nach dem anderen. Sie ist aber nicht als Telefonjob angelegt, sondern als Einstieg ins Partner Management — eigene Partner, Ende zu Ende, von Erstkontakt bis laufender Betreuung. Wie schnell das geht, hängt an dir, nicht an einem Kalender. Konkret: ANRUFEN, NICHT ABTELEFONIEREN: Du stellst das neue Produkt bei Bestandspartnern vor. Nicht Skript vom Blatt, sondern ein Gespräch, das beim Gegenüber ankommt. DEN PITCH WEITERENTWICKELN: Du merkst, welcher Einstieg funktioniert und welcher Einwand immer wieder kommt. Du behältst das nicht für dich, du änderst den Leitfaden. ZUHÖREN UND ZURÜCKSPIELEN: Was Partner am Telefon sagen, ist die ehrlichste Rückmeldung, die wir zum Produkt bekommen. Du bist die direkteste Leitung dorthin und nutzt sie. BEZIEHUNG STATT KONTAKTLISTE: Du übernimmst einen festen Kreis von Partnern. Nach drei Monaten kennen die deinen Namen, nicht unsere Rufnummer. SAUBER NACHHALTEN: Was besprochen wurde, landet nachvollziehbar in Hubspot, damit das Team damit weiterarbeiten kann. Dein Talent SUSTAINABILITY: Du interessierst dich sehr für Klimaschutz und Nachhaltigkeit und willst mehr darüber lernen und bewegen WORKING STUDENT: Du befindest dich aktuell in einem Studium und bringst idealerweise erste praktische Erfahrungen mit, zum Beispiel durch Praktika oder ehrenamtliches Engagement AM TELEFON ZU HAUSE: Du hast schon mal jemanden am Telefon von etwas überzeugt — im Job, im Verein, im Nebenjob, egal. AUF DEN PUNKT, OHNE KALT ZU WIRKEN: Du sagst in drei Sätzen, wofür andere zehn brauchen, und klingst dabei trotzdem wie ein Mensch. Handwerksbetriebe haben keine Zeit für Marketing-Sprache und merken sofort, wenn jemand welche spricht. ZUVERLÄSSIG, NICHT VERHANDELBAR: Zugesagter Rückruf am Donnerstag heißt Donnerstag. Das ist bei uns Grundvoraussetzung, keine Stärke. DU BRINGST WAS ZURÜCK: Nach fünfzig Gesprächen hast du eine Meinung dazu, was funktioniert. Du sagst sie, ohne dass wir danach fragen müssen. DEUTSCH AUF MUTTERSPRACHNIVEAU: Unsere Partner sind deutsche Handwerksbetriebe. Das Gespräch läuft auf Deutsch, inklusive Zwischentöne und Dialekt am anderen Ende. MINDESTENS 6 MONATE ZEIT: Kürzer lohnt sich für keinen von uns beiden. Bis du richtig gut in diesen Gesprächen bist, vergehen Wochen. Unser Angebot Wachstum & Kultur Werde Teil eines Teams, das nicht nur fachlich durchstartet, sondern aktiv eine gesunde und nachhaltige Unternehmenskultur lebt. Bei uns zählt das Miteinander genauso viel wie der Erfolg. Impact & Awareness Deine Stimme hat Gewicht, im Büro und darüber hinaus. Neben deinem regulären Urlaub bekommst du zusätzliche freie Tage für Klimaaktivismus, Demos oder Projekte, die dir am Herzen liegen. Flexibilität & Vertrauen Gestalte deinen Arbeitsalltag nach deinem Rhythmus. Nutze unsere Flexdays, um mobil zu arbeiten – egal ob von zu Hause oder unterwegs innerhalb Deutschlands, immer in Absprache mit deinem Team. Extra B

description: About Seamflow Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. It's the invisible layer that keeps the physical economy safe, and it still runs on Word documents, PDFs, spreadsheets and email. Seamflow is the software layer for that industry. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files. Where we are: Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed, co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze. Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists. The team Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further. The role A Front End Design Engineer thinks in finished interfaces, not mockups or components in isolation. A technical reviewer at a notified body spends their day inside a 400-page technical file, cross-referencing clauses, checking test reports against standards, and deciding whether a medical device is safe to sell. Today they do that in Word, Acrobat and a spreadsheet someone built in 2011. The interface they use decides how fast they work and whether they trust the AI sitting next to them. You own that interface. Layout, typography, interaction, motion, the design system underneath it, and the React that ships it. You decide how a reviewer sees a finding, how they correct a model that got it wrong, and how a hundred fields of dense regulatory data become something a person can actually read. You sketch it, build it, ship it, then sit next to someone using it and find out what you got wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week. What we're looking for We care far more about taste and engineering strength than about matching a list of tools. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in React, Svelte, Vue or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, craft and speed are not. What we're actually screening for: You've designed and built an interface that real people used every day. Not a Dribbble shot, not a component library nobody adopted. Something that shipped, got used, and got better. You have taste, and you can defend it. Typography, spacing, motion, hierarchy. You notice when something is a few pixels off and you can explain why it matters. You build the whole thing. Design, frontend, the state and data it sits on. You don't hand the code to someone else once the Figma is done, and you don't hand the design to someone else once the code is. You can design for density. Expert users, complex workflows, hundreds of fields on a screen. Making that clear is much harder than making a landing page beautiful. You go to the source. title: AI Content Engineer
description: Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call. Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data. We're hiring one person to own content at Soda, end to end. Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues. The Role The website. Technical blogs, webinars, and product videos. Your own content and following. One person cannot hand-make all of that. So you'll build the system that can. That isn't a stretch goal or a second phase - we don't think the job exists without it. You'll join the Growth team reporting to a co-founder. What you might call yourself.  Content engineer, technical content marketer, growth engineer, marketing engineer, GTM engineer, developer advocate, technical writer who got bored, or nothing in particular. We've seen this job posted under every one of those. We don't care what's on your CV. You need to be able to write and you need to be able to build, and almost nobody can do both. Why this is a real problem and not a content calendar.  The expertise is already in the building. Founders who have argued about this category for a decade. Customer engineers who spend their week inside broken pipelines at Fortune 500s. Customers who will tell you things nobody has published anywhere. Almost none of it gets written down, and what does get out is hand-made, one piece at a time, by people who have other jobs. Your job is to get it out of their heads and onto the internet, at a volume that is only possible with a machine behind it. Taste is the bar.  Anti-slop is the whole point. An engine that ships slop faster has negative value, and most of them do. We're hiring for the judgment to look at an accurate, competent, lifeless draft and bin it - then work out what the pipeline did wrong and fix it. The engine has to write in distinct voices: a founder sounds nothing like a customer engineer, and the output should sound like them, not like a model. Your own profile and following is part of how we'll know it works. If it can't make  you  sound good, it won't make anyone else sound good either. What this is not.  You'll write code every day, but this is not a software engineering job. We're not hiring you to build product, and if you're a backend, data, or platform engineer looking for your next engineering role, this isn't it. It's also not a traditional marketing or DevRel role: no agency to brief and no conference circuit. Requirements You can write, and you can tell good writing from bad : send us something you wrote that a technical audience actually read. The most important line in this ad. Serious prompt engineering : multi-step LLM pipelines with structured outputs and evals, not chatting with a model. You know why the naive version produces slop. 3+ years building things that go to market : technical content, growth engineering, marketing engineering, GTM engineering, DevRel, marketing ops, RevOps, or a founder background. Nobody agrees what to call this job yet. Titles vary; portfolios don't. Enough code to be autonomous : Python or TypeScript, APIs, webhooks, a database. Nothing should be blocked waiting for an engineer. We build agentically here - Claude Code, MCP servers, and agent skills are the daily workflow. Enough data fluency to be credible : you're writing for Staff Data Engineers and CDOs. You can hold your own on pipelines, data quality, and warehouses. Generalist instinct : you find the constraint and fix it, and you'd rather build the workflow than do the task fifteen more times. Independence : you
